Teglas Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Téglás, Hungary

Not demolished. Téglás's Jewish community, first documented in the mid-19th century with a synagogue, mikveh, and butcher's house built around that time, grew from 42 residents in 1880 to 183 by 1941. Rabbis Israel Paneth and Yisrael Mandel led the community before it joined Hajdúböszörmény's larger jurisdiction in 1885, remaining also affiliated with Gyulahalom and Búcsúháza; a second synagogue followed. Many Téglás Jews found success in alcohol production, winemaking, and steam-engine manufacturing; a wave of 1911 emigrants founded one of Canada's largest supermarket chains. In 1941, young men were sent for forced labor; following 1944's German occupation, residents were transported to the Bácsipuszta Ghetto alongside Hajdúsámson and Vámospércs Jews, then deported to Auschwitz on May 25. This cemetery's oldest tombstone dates to 1883, its newest to 1938.
